caption: The video captures a close, mostly fixed view of a metal saucepan sitting on a gas-stove burner, its blue flame steady beneath a pot of vigorously boiling water. A person's right hand holds an INKBIRD digital thermometer over the rim, the metal probe dipped into the churning liquid, indicating an ongoing measurement. The LCD's digits climb progressively, stepping from a transitional reading up through values around 85.9, then 95.4, then 98.6, and finally settling near 99.7 degrees Celsius. Throughout, bubbles form, rise, and burst at the surface while steam drifts upward, and the hand and thermometer remain in essentially the same position with only slight tremor. The pot, burner grates, and surrounding stove keep their relative positions, so the visible motion comes mainly from the changing temperature display and the restless boiling water rather than any significant camera travel.
relations: Steady blue flame beneath the saucepan -> vigorous boiling water continuously forms, rises, and bursts bubbles.
Submerged thermometer probe in hot liquid -> LCD digits progressively climb toward a stable near-boiling temperature.
Heat from boiling water -> steam drifts upward while the holding hand remains mostly fixed.
Fixed relative positions of pot and grates -> visible motion is driven by the changing display and restless water.
